title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section (6) on relatively smooth schemes in characteristic p. Let X/S be smooth of relative dimension n, X^{p/S} = X^{(p)} the Frobenius twist, and F_{X/S}: X -> X^{(p)} the relative Frobenius. F_{X/S} is finite, locally free, radicial and surjective.

Step 1 (justification). Grothendieck must justify an isomorphism Omega_{X^{(p)}} ≅ Λ. Here Λ is presumably the target of the abstract Cartier operation defined earlier in the notes, for a morphism admitting a p-basis. He sketches two arguments.
- It suffices to check fibre by fibre. On a fibre, X_s -> X_s^{(p)} is finite between regular schemes of the same dimension.
- Alternatively, X has locally a p-basis over X^{(p)}. Since X is locally of finite type over S, this is equivalent to Omega^1_{X/S} being locally free, which holds by smoothness.

Step 2 (the Cartier operation). Hence the general Cartier operation of the earlier sections specialises to the classical one, C~: F_{X/S*}(Z Omega^•_{X/S}) -> Omega^•_{X^{(p)}/S}. In top degree n every form is closed, so this gives C~: F_{X/S*} ω_{X/S} -> ω_{X^{(p)}/S}, where ω is the relative dualizing sheaf.

Step 3 (Theorem 3). This top-degree Cartier map equals the trace map Tr_{F_{X/S}} attached by duality to the finite flat morphism F_{X/S} between S-smooth schemes.

Step 4 (concrete form via residues). Let f_1,...,f_n be local sections cutting out a closed subscheme Z ⊂ X finite over S. Their twists f~_i = f_i ⊗ 1 on X^{(p)} cut out Z~ ⊂ X^{(p)}. The pullbacks F*(f~_i) = f_i^p cut out Z' ⊂ X, also finite over S. The theorem is then equivalent (continued on the next page) to the residue-symbol identity
  res[C~ω / f~_1,...,f~_n] = res[ω / f_1^p,...,f_n^p].
This follows from the transitivity of residue symbols under the finite map F together with the trace. On the next page this specialises, for curves, to res C~ϖ = res ϖ, and for perfect S to (res Cϖ)^p = res ϖ, which is Tate's formula.

Purpose: identify Cartier's operator with the duality trace of Frobenius, and so link Cartier theory to Grothendieck duality and residues.
errors: The identification 'Omega_{X^{p/S}} ≅ Λ' is not explained on this page; the definition of Λ is on earlier pages. The fibre-by-fibre argument is only gestured at.
Statement of Theorem 3 writes the trace as f_{X/S*}; it means Tr_{F_{X/S}}: F_{X/S*}ω_{X/S} -> ω_{X^{(p)}/S}. This is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.
The page stops before the residue formula is stated or proved; no proof of Theorem 3 is given here.

ideas.what: For X/S locally of finite type in char p, X has a local p-basis over X^{(p)} iff Omega^1_{X/S} is locally free.
Classical Cartier operation C~: F_*(ZΩ^•_{X/S}) -> Ω^•_{X^{(p)}/S} for smooth X/S.
Theorem 3: the top-degree Cartier operator equals the Grothendieck-duality trace of the relative Frobenius.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Tate 1968 for curves; standard in Frobenius-splitting literature (Mehta–Ramanathan, Brion–Kumar §1.3)
ideas.where_published: Brion–Kumar, Frobenius Splitting Methods (2005), §1.3; Lipman's work on residues/traces

ideas.what: Residue-symbol form: res[C~ω/f~_1..f~_n] = res[ω/f_1^p..f_n^p]; for curves res Cϖ = (res ϖ)^{1/p}.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of Cartier operator with Grothendieck residue symbol
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (curves, 1968); higher-dimensional versions in Kunz, Lipman, Hübl
ideas.where_published: Tate, Ann. Sci. ENS 1968; Kunz, Kähler Differentials; Hartshorne RD for residue symbols

missed.claim: An early (c. 1972) explicit statement by Grothendieck that the top-degree Cartier operator is the duality trace of relative Frobenius over an arbitrary base S, with a residue-symbol reformulation. The result itself is now standard folklore, so this is mainly of historical value: it predates the usual Frobenius-splitting references.
missed.quote: Théorème 3 L'homomorphisme précédent est l'homomorphisme trace (ou de Cartier) f_{X/S*} associé au morphisme fini f_{X/S} : X → X^{p/S} de schémas lisses sur S.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the foundational fact behind Cartier modules and F-singularities (Blickle–Schwede). It is of historical interest for attribution, not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The identification of the Cartier operator with the trace of Frobenius, and its residue form, is well known (Tate for curves; folklore and Frobenius-splitting literature in general). The page is a clean early relative formulation but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Insertion under first line likely reads: 'où X_s → X_s^{p/s} est fini, X_s (lisse) régulier, de même dim que source'.
'f_{X/S*}' throughout should be read as F_{X/S*} (pushforward/trace along relative Frobenius), the handwritten script F.
'en effet [?], équivalemment [?]' probably 'en effet, grâce au fait que X est loc. de t.f. sur S'.
'de vérifier' at start of line 2 is 'de vérifier fibre par fibre'; 'Théorème 3' heading is boxed/bracketed in margin.
